gold_rationale: A single 6-OHDA mouse motor-behavior result is preclinical evidence only and does not establish clinical efficacy in patients. The stated claim ('therefore proven clinically effective') is an overclaim: the correct classification is Contradicted (the proof claim is false), or at most Unsupported for the underlying compound. The appraisal must penalize the preclinical-to-clinical inference and state what human evidence would be required.
required_concepts: what evidence would be required (human RCT, PK, safety)
red_flags: endorses the claim that a mouse result proves clinical efficacy
classifies as Supported or Partially supported
fails to identify the preclinical-to-clinical overclaim
treats animal motor improvement as clinical proof

criteria.name: correct_classification
criteria.description: Reaches 'Contradicted' (or 'Unsupported') and rejects the proof claim.

criteria.name: evidence_use
criteria.description: Correctly characterizes the single preclinical study and its limits.

criteria.name: uncertainty_handling
criteria.description: States the human evidence required to support a clinical claim.
